decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up right-arm approach to the central coin; bank is on the right. Small initial lift and wrist rotation to preserve configuration.
Advance inward and forward while pitching the right gripper toward an overhead coin grasp, leaving the left arm parked.
Continue toward the coin with an overhead wrist orientation; use moderate increments and monitor joint continuity.
Bring the right wrist over the central holder while finishing the downward approach orientation; keep clearance above the coin.
Align above the holder with open fingers; finish overhead rotation before the final small descent.
Use the wrist view to center the coin between the open fingers, approaching the top edge slowly.
Fine-align the finger closing direction with the coin's faces and lower a few millimeters, using the wrist image rather than assuming grasp success.
Correct the observed wrist-image yaw error and lateral offset before closing; the coin is still on its holder.
Center the coin across the finger gap and raise slightly to grasp its exposed edge rather than the holder.
Coin is visually centered in the wrist view. Close the right fingers around its exposed edge, with only a tiny yaw correction.
Allow full closure to settle, then test retention with a short vertical lift while keeping the gripper closed.
Lift vertically clear of the holder by about nine centimeters, keeping the coin clamped and checking retention visually.
The coin remains in the holder after the lift, so the grasp missed. Reopen and descend for a slightly deeper edge grasp.
Lower another small amount and correct the coin's slight rightward offset in the wrist view before retrying closure.
Adjust along the coin plane to bring its exposed rim to the pinch point, then partially close while checking alignment.
Make a final small planar alignment so the coin lies at the finger tips, then finish closing without lifting.
Test the deeper grasp with a gentle vertical lift, holding the fingers fully closed and watching for separation from the holder.
Continue the retention check vertically; the coin's relation to the fingertips is still uncertain, so avoid lateral transport until separation is clear.
The coin stayed on the holder. Retry with an open gripper, correcting the small sideways miss and returning to the deeper grasp height.
The coin is laterally centered; shift along its plane to place the exposed edge deeper between the finger tips before closing.
Center the visible coin rim at the pinch point and close gradually. Hold stationary to let closure settle before another lift test.
Finish closing on the centered coin and dwell at the grasp pose; do not transport until retention is visible.
Test retention with a short straight lift, keeping the coin clamped and observing whether it separates from the holder.
Raise further to distinguish a retained coin from one left in the holder; maintain a closed gripper and no lateral motion.
The coin is still in the holder. Reopen and approach lower, as the earlier pinch did not engage the coin.
Lower the open fingertips farther onto the exposed coin and correct its small rightward offset; begin a slow closure only at the deeper pose.
At the deeper height, advance slightly along the coin plane to align the rim with the finger contact region and complete closure.
Hold the deeper grasp pose completely still and keep full closure commanded so the fingers can settle around the coin.
Test the settled grasp with a very slow vertical lift while maintaining full closure.
Continue the gentle lift to check whether the coin clears its holder; keep the pinch closed.
The coin now appears between the fingers. Lift above the holder with a small rightward offset to verify separation and retention.
Coin is visibly clear of the empty holder and retained. Raise for bank clearance and move right while aligning the coin plane with the slot.
Transport the retained coin toward the right-side bank with clearance, finishing the slot-parallel yaw alignment.
Move the coin above the bank's slot while maintaining overhead clearance and a closed grip; refine from the wrist view next.
Shift over the visually estimated slot center, holding height until the slot is visible around the coin.
Align the coin laterally with the visible slot and begin a small controlled descent, keeping the coin closed in the gripper.
Coin and slot are laterally aligned. Make a small lengthwise correction while lowering toward insertion depth.
Correct the small lateral parallax error seen beside the slot and lower the coin another centimeter, keeping it securely pinched.
Make a very small slot-angle and lengthwise correction while easing the coin downward; monitor for slipping or edge contact.
Center the coin within the slot width, ease it a few millimeters deeper, then release while holding the wrist still.
Let the released coin settle into the slot, then begin a short upward clearance move with the fingers fully open.
The coin has disappeared into the slot and the fingers are empty. Withdraw with clearance and begin returning both wrists to origin, preserving elbow-up continuity.
Continue withdrawing to the right-arm home pose with the gripper open; smoothly unwind the wrist and lower away from the bank.
Return the empty right gripper toward origin in small continuous steps, staying clear of the bank.
Ease the right arm into its original pose with an open gripper, reducing the final approach increments.
